# CI Requirements Quality Checklist: Continuous Integration Pipeline

**Purpose**: A formal requirements-quality gate for the CI feature. It covers the merge gate,
pipeline security, dependency updates and static analysis, and is meant for the author to use
before `/speckit-tasks`.
**Created**: 2026-09-27
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md). Also reviews [plan.md](../plan.md), [research.md](../research.md) and [contracts/ci-checks.md](../contracts/ci-checks.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 - Does the spec define whether the checks run for pull requests that target branches other than `main`, such as a stacked branch on top of another feature branch? Or is limiting them to `main` an explicit exclusion? [Gap, Spec §FR-001]
- [x] CHK002 - Are the four stable check names written down in the spec itself, or only in the plan's contract? Is the rule "renaming a check requires updating the merge rule" a requirement? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, contracts/ci-checks.md]
- [x] CHK003 - Does the spec say where the "one declared source" of the runtime version lives, so that FR-006 can be checked without reading the plan? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006]
- [x] CHK004 - Does the spec require the test database version to stay in step with the local development environment in the same way FR-006 does for the runtime, or can the two drift? [Gap, Spec §FR-003]
- [x] CHK005 - Does the spec define what should happen, and who is told, when the checks fail on `main` after a merge, beyond the failure being "visible"? [Gap, Spec §US1 scenario 6]
- [x] CHK006 - Are the permissions that jobs may be granted beyond read-only listed, or does FR-013 give only one example ("such as reporting security findings")? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013]
- [x] CHK007 - Does the spec require approval before workflows run for first-time outside contributors' pull requests, or does that rule appear only in research.md #9? [Gap, Spec §FR-012]
- [x] CHK008 - Is the trade-off of the lockfile workaround stated as a spec-level assumption with its compensating controls? The trade-off is that the package manager stops checking its own version. [Gap, Assumption, Spec §Clarifications, research.md #2]
- [x] CHK009 - Does the spec state when the lockfile workaround should be reverted, for example when the upstream dependency-graph fix ships? [Gap, Spec §FR-020]
- [x] CHK010 - Does the spec say how major-version library and base-image updates are handled? FR-021 covers only minor and patch grouping. [Gap, Spec §FR-019, §FR-021]
- [x] CHK011 - Are supply-chain protections for update proposals (a waiting period before adopting newly published versions) written as a requirement, or do they exist only in the plan? [Gap, Spec §FR-019, research.md #8]
- [x] CHK012 - Does the spec say where the contributor documentation lives? Milestone 7 owns the contribution guide, and FR-024 has to fit around that. [Completeness, Spec §FR-024]
- [x] CHK013 - Does FR-025 list every new mitigation that the Threat Model update must record? The list should include the lockfile-format guard, the vulnerability audit and the no-bypass merge rule, not only FR-012 to FR-014 and FR-019. [Completeness, Spec §FR-025]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK014 - Is "maximum run time" given as a value, or a ceiling, in the spec? Or is FR-010 satisfied by any timeout at all? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK015 - Is "throwaway, non-secret" defined with criteria a reviewer can apply? For example: grants no access outside the ephemeral run, and matches the published development defaults. [Clarity, Spec §FR-012]
- [x] CHK016 - Is "style rules" in the US1 narrative defined? The plan limits the style check to linting and defers format checking. Does the spec reflect that? [Ambiguity, Spec §US1, §FR-001, research.md #11]
- [x] CHK017 - Is "an unreadable format" in FR-020 defined precisely enough to guard mechanically, for example "more than one document in the lockfile"? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020]
- [x] CHK018 - Is "without waiting for the regular schedule" given a latency expectation, or is any time before the next scheduled cycle acceptable? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020]
- [x] CHK019 - Is the condition in FR-018 ("if the analysis tool supports it") resolved to a firm requirement, now that research has confirmed support? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-018, research.md #3]
- [x] CHK020 - Is it clear whether "every push to the main branch" in FR-001 still matters, given that FR-008 now rejects direct pushes? Pushes would come only from merges. [Clarity, Spec §FR-001, §FR-008]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK021 - Is FR-023's list of settings "with no file-based equivalent" consistent with research.md #9? The research adds turning off the default analysis setup, a read-only default token, and fork approval. [Conflict, Spec §FR-023, research.md #9]
- [x] CHK022 - Does the Assumptions bullet on outward-facing settings changes list the same settings as FR-023 and research.md #9? [Consistency, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK023 - Is FR-019(b), "propose updates for the base image", consistent with the plan's decision to ignore base-image major versions and pin by digest? Is that exclusion recorded in the spec? [Conflict, Spec §FR-019, research.md #5]
- [x] CHK024 - Is FR-014 (immutable references for third-party steps) consistent with how the CI test database image is referenced? The plan uses a movable tag for the service container image. [Conflict, Spec §FR-014, contracts/ci-checks.md]
- [x] CHK025 - Are FR-020a ("at least weekly") and the plan (daily) consistent? Is the minimum frequency the one intended? [Consistency, Spec §FR-020a, research.md #2]
- [x] CHK026 - Does the merge gate definition (Key Entities, FR-008) consistently exclude static analysis and the audit from the required checks? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, §FR-017, §FR-020a]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK027 - Is "a typical pull request" in SC-003 defined, and is "dependency caches are warm" a condition that can be observed? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]
- [x] CHK028 - Can "other checks fail only where they legitimately process the same broken code" in SC-002 be judged objectively? For example, is there a stated expected-failure set for each canary? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002, quickstart.md §2]
- [x] CHK029 - Is SC-006's "before deciding whether to merge" measurable, given that analysis may finish after the required checks? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006]
- [x] CHK030 - Is SC-009's "a non-zero number of library dependencies" strong enough to detect a partial parse? The quickstart expects roughly the lockfile's package count. [Measurability, Conflict, Spec §SC-009, quickstart.md §6]
- [x] CHK031 - Is "an explicit up-to-date status" in SC-007 tied to an observable signal that a reviewer can locate? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007]
- [x] CHK032 - Can "on the first attempt" in SC-008 be verified with a defined procedure and a defined kind of participant? [Measurability, Spec §SC-008]
- [x] CHK033 - Is there an acceptance criterion for FR-015 (no secrets in logs) that a reviewer can check? [Gap, Measurability, Spec §FR-015]

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK034 - Are recovery requirements complete for the emergency merge-rule disable? That means who may do it, when the rule must be restored, and whether the event must be recorded. [Coverage, Recovery, Spec §FR-008, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK035 - Is recovery specified for an update proposal that fails because a transitive dependency was published too recently? For example, when and how it is regenerated. [Coverage, Recovery, Spec §Edge Cases, research.md #8]
- [x] CHK036 - Are requirements defined for triaging static-analysis findings? That covers who triages, whether a dismissal needs a reason, and any expected turnaround. [Coverage, Spec §FR-017, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK037 - Does the spec address the scenario where the hosting platform turns off scheduled runs after a long period of repository inactivity? That would silently stop FR-016's and FR-020a's schedules. [Gap, Exception Flow, research.md #9]
- [x] CHK038 - Are requirements defined for pull requests opened by the update tool itself? They should get the same no-secrets, read-only treatment as fork pull requests. [Coverage, Spec §FR-012, §US3 scenario 4]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK039 - Does the spec cover a merge where every check passed on the pull request's latest commit but its base is out of date with `main`? Is not requiring branches to be up to date an accepted, documented risk? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-008, research.md #9]
- [x] CHK040 - Is the behavior specified when the builder and runtime stages of the container definition declare different runtime versions? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-006, contracts/ci-checks.md]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK041 - Is the assumption that a maintainer with admin rights is available to apply and restore repository settings recorded, along with what happens if one isn't? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK042 - Is the gap between the declared minimum runtime (`>=20`, end of life) and the single tested runtime (22) recorded as an accepted risk, with a follow-up owner or milestone? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK043 - Are the external upstream issues this spec depends on referenced from the spec, so a reader can see what would change the decisions? These are the dependency-graph parser fix and pnpm's release-age resolver fix. [Dependency, Traceability, Spec §Clarifications]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Items marked `[Conflict]` (CHK021, CHK023, CHK024, CHK030) point to places where the spec and the plan disagree. Resolve these first, before `/speckit-tasks`, by editing whichever side is wrong.
